Bayesian VAR

Source: vignettes/bayesian-var.Rmd
bayesian-var.Rmd

bvarm() fits a conjugate Normal-inverse-Wishart BVAR with the prior of Giannone, Lenza and Primiceri (2015), specified by prior_minnesota():

  • Minnesota shrinkage with overall tightness lambda and lag decay alpha;
  • sum-of-coefficients (soc) and single-unit-root (sur) dummy-observation priors, each of which can be dropped by passing NULL;
  • the inverse-Wishart scale psi (AR(p) residual variances by default);
  • prior mean of the own first lag delta (1 for levels, 0 for growth rates).

Every hyperparameter is c(mode, sd, min, max) of a gamma hyperprior. The character vector hyper selects which are estimated; the rest stay fixed.

Fixed hyperparameters: exact posterior draws

With hyper = character(0) the posterior is sampled exactly (no MCMC, so nburn is unused).

pr <- prior_minnesota(lambda = 0.2, soc = NULL, sur = NULL, hyper = character(0))
fit0 <- bvarm(y, p = 2, prior = pr, ndraw = 1000)
fit0
#> <bvarm> niw-minnesota BVAR(2), K = 3, 1000 posterior draws
#> log marginal likelihood: -442.40252
#> 
#> posterior mean of B:
#>                 inflation unemployment    rate
#> inflation.l1       1.3529       0.0001  0.3714
#> unemployment.l1   -0.2046       1.2009 -0.3936
#> rate.l1           -0.0152      -0.0229  0.8756
#> inflation.l2      -0.3552       0.0322 -0.2770
#> unemployment.l2    0.1390      -0.2991  0.4091
#> rate.l2            0.0149       0.0441  0.0273
#> const              0.3923       0.3513  0.0847

Hierarchical hyperparameters

By default lambda, soc and sur are estimated: the mode is found by optim() and a compiled Metropolis sampler with adaptive scale draws the hyperparameters; coefficients and covariances are then drawn directly.

fit <- bvarm(y, p = 2, ndraw = 1000, nburn = 500)
fit
#> <bvarm> niw-minnesota BVAR(2), K = 3, 1000 posterior draws
#> log marginal likelihood: -407.08851
#> hyperparameters (posterior mean [5%, 95%]); MH acceptance 0.481
#>          mean     5%    95%
#> lambda 0.6172 0.4152 0.9069
#> soc    0.3508 0.2055 0.5650
#> sur    0.5829 0.2039 1.1002
#> 
#> posterior mean of B:
#>                 inflation unemployment    rate
#> inflation.l1       1.5236       0.0219  0.5112
#> unemployment.l1   -0.2497       1.3276 -0.6021
#> rate.l1           -0.0451      -0.0205  0.7998
#> inflation.l2      -0.5293       0.0016 -0.4111
#> unemployment.l2    0.2138      -0.4036  0.6214
#> rate.l2            0.0455       0.0421  0.1059
#> const              0.2260       0.2472  0.0300
colMeans(fit$hyper)
#>    lambda       soc       sur 
#> 0.6171950 0.3508325 0.5828661
fit$accept       # Metropolis acceptance rate
#> [1] 0.481
fit$logml        # log marginal likelihood at the hyperparameter mode
#> [1] -407.0885

Use hyper = "full" to also estimate alpha and psi. The marginal likelihood can be used to compare prior settings or lag lengths.

c(p1 = bvarm(y, p = 1, ndraw = 200, nburn = 200)$logml,
  p2 = fit$logml)
#>        p1        p2 
#> -460.7686 -407.0885

Posterior summaries, IRFs and forecasts

summary() gives posterior means, standard deviations and 5/95% quantiles of B. The draws element is a varm_draws object, the same container used by the bootstrap, so all identification schemes work.

s <- summary(fit)
round(s$mean[1:3, ], 3)
#>                 inflation unemployment   rate
#> inflation.l1        1.524        0.022  0.511
#> unemployment.l1    -0.250        1.328 -0.602
#> rate.l1            -0.045       -0.020  0.800
max(stability(fit))   # largest eigenvalue modulus across draws
#> [1] 1.014878
ir <- irf(fit, id = id_chol(), horizon = 16)
ir
#> <varm IRF> K = 3, horizon 0..16, id = chol, bands: 68%/90%
plot(ir, shocks = "rate")

Sign restrictions apply to Bayesian draws as well.

S <- matrix(0, 3, 3, dimnames = list(colnames(y), c("mp", "s2", "s3")))
S["rate", "mp"] <- 1; S["inflation", "mp"] <- -1
irs <- irf(fit, id = id_sign(S, horizon = 2, maxtry = 2000), horizon = 12)
irs$accept_rate
#> [1] 0.3506311
fc <- forecast(fit, h = 8)
round(fc$mean, 2)
#>      inflation unemployment rate
#> [1,]      2.72         4.87 4.64
#> [2,]      2.65         4.96 4.49
#> [3,]      2.64         5.03 4.38
#> [4,]      2.68         5.08 4.33
#> [5,]      2.71         5.12 4.31
#> [6,]      2.75         5.16 4.29
#> [7,]      2.80         5.20 4.31
#> [8,]      2.84         5.22 4.29

fevd() and hd() (median over ndraw posterior draws) are available as well.

Not yet implemented

Stochastic-volatility, stochastic-search variable selection and other shrinkage priors, time-varying-parameter VARs, non-conjugate and independent Normal-Wishart priors, Gibbs samplers other than the Minnesota/GLP one, and factor-augmented VARs. Although the package DESCRIPTION mentions them, there is no code behind them yet.
